items.stem: What does a variable store in a program?
options: A value that can be used later

items.stem: Which structure repeats an action while a condition remains true?
A function returns x + 2. What does it return when x is 3?
A test expects 4 but receives 5. What does this result establish?
options: The program has a security flaw
The tested behavior differs from the expectation

items.stem: A list has three entries at indexes 0, 1, and 2. Code tries to read index 3. What is the most direct fix?
options: Read index 2 when the last entry is needed

items.stem: What identifies a device interface on an IP network?
What is DNS mainly used for?
Two devices use 192.168.1.10/24 and 192.168.1.20/24 on the same LAN. What can they normally do without a router?
A device can ping its router but cannot resolve example.com. Which service should be checked first?
One laptop loses Wi-Fi while nearby laptops remain connected. What is the best first check?
options: Disable the firewall for all users
Check that laptop’s Wi-Fi state and local connection

items.stem: Authentication answers which question?
What does least privilege mean?
options: Give only access needed for a task
Share one account across a team

items.stem: An account has many failed logins followed by one successful login from a new location. What is a reasonable first interpretation?
A colleague asks for your password to complete their task. What should you do?
options: Post it in the team chat
Decline and use an approved access request

items.stem: A suspicious endpoint alert appears. Which response best preserves evidence while following procedure?
options: Immediately wipe the device without authorization
Record details and escalate under the incident playbook

items.stem: What is a missing value in a dataset?
options: A field without an observed value

items.stem: For values 2, 4, and 6, what is the mean?
Monthly users rise from 100 to 120. What is the percentage increase relative to 100?
A chart shows sales rose in June. Can it alone prove a new website caused the rise?
options: No, other factors could explain it

items.stem: A dataset contains duplicate orders. What should happen before counting unique orders?
options: Use only the first ten rows
Identify duplicates using a reliable order ID

items.stem: What is a primary key used for?
What does a foreign key usually represent?
options: A reference to a row in another table

items.stem: A query uses WHERE status = 'active'. Which rows should it return?
options: Only rows whose status is active

items.stem: Each student can enroll in many courses, and each course has many students. What table is usually needed?
options: An enrollment table linking student and course IDs
A single course-name field in student

items.stem: A report counts the same order twice after joining orders to order_items. What is the likely reason?
options: One order has multiple matching item rows

items.stem: Why should a form field have a visible label?
options: People can understand what to enter

items.stem: What is a usability test mainly used to observe?
options: How people complete tasks with an interface

items.stem: Two users cannot find the Submit button because it appears only after horizontal scrolling. Which change directly addresses the evidence?
options: Keep the action visible within the layout

items.stem: A form shows “Error” after submission. Which message is more useful?
options: “Enter a valid email address in Email.”

items.stem: A redesign looks cleaner, but users now take longer to finish a task. What should the team do next?
options: Keep it because it looks cleaner
Observe where users slow down and test a revision

items.stem: What is a hypothesis in troubleshooting?
Why reproduce a reported problem?
options: To observe conditions and check a proposed cause
To prove the user is wrong

items.stem: An app fails only after a new configuration is enabled. Which clue is most relevant?
options: The configuration change and failure timing

items.stem: Two possible causes are a bad network route and a stopped app service. Which check best separates them?
options: Test route reachability and service status separately

items.stem: A proposed fix does not change the symptom. What is the best next step?
options: Revisit the hypothesis and collect new evidence

items.stem: What is an operating system service?
options: A background process that provides a function

items.stem: What do file permissions control?
options: Who may read, change, or execute a file

items.stem: A server shows disk use at 99%. Which symptom is plausible?
Before changing a production service setting, what is a safe preparation step?
options: Record the current setting and rollback plan

items.stem: A web service stops after a restart; the host responds to ping. What should be checked next?
What does separation of concerns aim to do?
options: Keep different responsibilities in appropriate components
Put all logic in one function

items.stem: What is an interface between components?
options: An agreed way they exchange data or behavior

items.stem: A checkout page formats prices and also calculates tax rules. Where should reusable tax calculation usually live?
options: In every page as copied code
Only in the button color rule

items.stem: A form sends data to an API, which stores it in a database. Which sequence matches the data flow?
The same validation rule is copied across three pages and changes often. What is the most maintainable small change?
options: Move the shared rule into one reusable function

items.stem: Why record the exact error message?
options: It provides a clue that can be checked

items.stem: What does a reproducible failure mean?
options: Only one user can report it
The same steps can trigger it again

items.stem: A service error starts at 10:02, two minutes after a deployment. What should the investigator inspect first?
A site fails for one user but works for others. Which first test helps narrow scope?
options: Try another browser or device for that user
Assume the site works for everyone

items.stem: A fix appears to restore service. What best verifies resolution?
options: Repeat the failing steps and monitor for recurrence

tasks.title: Software development
tasks.prompt: A function meant to return the larger of two numbers returns the smaller one when a = 8 and b = 3. Its logic is: if (a > b) return b; otherwise return a. Describe the defect, a correction, and one test you would run.

tasks.title: Networking
tasks.prompt: A laptop has IP 192.168.10.25/24 and gateway 192.168.10.1. It can ping 192.168.10.1 but cannot open example.com. A second laptop on the same Wi-Fi can open it. Give one likely cause, a check that could confirm it, and a correction if confirmed.

tasks.title: Cybersecurity
tasks.prompt: A sample alert shows ten failed sign-ins for one account, then a successful sign-in from a new location. You do not know whether the user is traveling. Explain what you would check, what evidence you would preserve, and when you would escalate. Do not assume compromise is certain.

tasks.title: Data analytics
tasks.prompt: A club reports 80 sign-ups in June and 100 in July, then says its new poster caused a 25% increase. Calculate the percentage change and explain one reason the cause claim needs more evidence.

tasks.title: Database administration
tasks.prompt: A report joins Orders(order_id, customer_id) with OrderItems(item_id, order_id). Order 42 has three items and appears three times. Explain why, describe a safe way to count orders, and name one check before changing a production query.

tasks.title: UI/UX and web development
tasks.prompt: Two students using a mobile application form missed the Submit button because it was off-screen to the right. Describe a layout change, one accessibility check, and a quick test with users to see whether the change helps.
